title: A decompression-bomb image pins every resize worker's CPU
source_note: Failure pattern (a small crafted input that expands enormously on decode, consuming CPU and memory per attempt - a decompression bomb, CWE-409) applied to an image-processing service. All services, asset ids, log lines, metrics, and timestamps are fabricated for evaluation.
incident_report: Since ~19:32 UTC image resizing is extremely slow platform-wide and the resize queue is huge. No deploys. CPU on the resize fleet is pinned.

signal_lines.msg: worker CPU 80%; several resize jobs running >30s (normal <500ms)
decode job for asset a91f exceeded 60s; image declares 48000x48000 px from a 40KB file
all workers busy on oversized-decode jobs; resize queue depth 9000; CPU pinned
operator added a max-decoded-dimension guard and blocklisted asset a91f; CPU recovering

ground_truth.root_cause: A user uploaded a decompression-bomb image: a ~40KB file that declares 48000x48000 pixel dimensions. image-resizer attempted to fully decode it, consuming enormous CPU and holding a worker for tens of seconds per attempt. The client retried the same asset ~140 times, so many workers were simultaneously stuck on oversized-decode jobs, CPU saturated, and the resize queue backed up for all users. There was no deploy - the trigger was the crafted input plus the absence of a decoded-size guard. Recovery required adding a max-decoded-dimension check and blocklisting the asset.
evidence_path: image-resizer resize jobs suddenly take >30s against a <500ms baseline and worker CPU climbs
image-resizer ERROR: a 40KB asset declares 48000x48000 px and its decode exceeds 60s
the same asset was resubmitted ~140 times by client retries
all workers become stuck on oversized-decode jobs; CPU pins and the queue grows to 9000
no deploy; recovery after a max-decoded-dimension guard is added and the asset is blocklisted
ground_truth.fix: Add a decoded-dimension / pixel-count limit before decoding and reject oversized images (done). Blocklist the offending asset, add per-job CPU and time budgets, and rate-limit repeated submissions of the same asset.
